To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in three dysmyelination mutants, myelin proteins are differentially expressed and may or may not assemble into myelin.

in the three mutants studied, the expression of the two major myelin proteins, MBP and PLP, is affected independently and that the failure to assemble these proteins into a stable membrane such as myelin may be due to the failure of the newly synthesized proteins to be incorporated into the membrane.

(1) the MBPs and the PLP are synthesized in the brains of the jimpy, shiverer, and quaking mutants, (2) synthesis of MBPs and/or PLP is reduced or absent in these mutants, (3) the MBPs are incorporated into a stable myelin membrane structure in the quaking and shiverer mutants, and (4) the MBPs fail to be incorporated into the myelin membrane structure of the jimpy mutants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of gene expression in the nervous system.
the expression of the myelin‐related proteins in the brains of three dysmyelinated mutants.
the regulation of myelin protein gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MBPs and the PLP are expressed in these three mutants, but their assembly into a stable membrane is affected.
the expression of MBP and PLP is not necessarily coupled, and that the assembly of these proteins into myelin is independent of their synthesis.
the MBPs and the PLP are not synthesized in the same manner in the brain and that the mutations in the jimpy, quaking and shiverer mutants affect these proteins independently.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MBPs are not synthesized at all in shiverer and are synthesized but not assembled into myelin (in jimpy and quaking).
in the jimpy, quaking and shiverer mutants the expression of the myelin proteins is affected in different ways, and that these differences are reflected in the myelin sheaths of the mutants.
the expression of the myelin proteins is under the control of at least two independent regulatory systems, one controlling the synthesis of MBPs and the other the synthesis of PLP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MBPs and proteolipids are not necessarily synthesized in the same cells and that the synthesis of one does not necessarily guarantee synthesis of the other.
in the jimpy mutant there is an absolute failure in the expression of PLP, whereas MBP synthesis is reduced to 26% of normal levels.
the MBP and PLP are not expressed in a coordinate manner in the dysmyelinating mutant mice.
